summary:
COMPROMISE on web-01 via the shared deploy account's password. Unauthorized password logins as deploy came from 64.227.126.70 (a DigitalOcean address that no staff member uses) about 60 times between Nov 1 and Nov 12, most recently 06:22 today. One successful deploy password login came from 73.162.47.18 on Nov 10. The sessions executed commands as deploy; sshd does not log commands, so what they ran is unknown. Deploy owns the web root and wp-config.php (mode 640), so the site's database password was readable to the attacker. I found no root escalation: no sudo commands by deploy other than the release, and root-only secrets (payments.ini, dump passphrase, backup password, offsite key) are root-only and were not read as far as I can tell. Not seen on db-01 or ci-01: no password logins for deploy from those IPs, and no logins from them at all.

CONTAINED / CHANGED (web-01 unless noted):
- Rotated the deploy password (rotate-secret deploy-password). Maria is locked out of deploy until the help desk delivers the new password (~8 min). Staff vault updated per the tool.
- Rotated app-db-password (rotate-secret). wp-config.php updated by the tool; site DB access verified as www-data; homepage and rentals return 200.
- Closed the password path for deploy: sshd Match User deploy PasswordAuthentication no, on web-01 AND ci-01. The CI release key still works; the release log on ci-01 shows release ok through 19:03.
- Removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync (a root shortcut the release does not use). deploy keeps larkspur-deploy and larkspur-restart only. Backup of the old sudoers at /root/larkspur.sudoers.bak.
- Locked the unlisted account jpark (Jun Park, not on the staff roster) on web-01 and ci-01 (passwd -l, nologin). It had dozens of failed password attempts from many internet addresses (e.g. 198.235.245.207, 103.149.253.198, 185.224.77.71, 148.251.74.97, 71.6.121.157); I saw no successful jpark login. Maria should confirm whether Jun Park needs an account and, if so, give it a key.
- Checked the untracked plugin files: inc/booking.php was hand-copied in April by Theo (the rentals booking box), inc/hours.php.bak is from Oct. Neither looks malicious.

CHECKED, NO COMPROMISE FOUND: db-01 (no unexpected logins, no unknown accounts, billing_app limited to billing schema from web-01 only, wp_larkspur limited to wordpress schema). ci-01 (release job, dumps, repository main unchanged at 883881f, only backups and staff keys).

NOT CHANGED, NEEDS MARIA: (1) Grafana (port 3000) and node exporter (9100) listen on the public address with no firewall rule; I did not close them because ops may use them remotely. (2) Deploy owns the web root, so anything running as deploy can rewrite the site; consider a separate owner. (3) Attacker's commands as deploy are not logged; consider reviewing web-01 for any backdoor the release would not overwrite (I found none in the plugin or web root by mtime and git status). (4) Staff sharing IP 24.30.29.136 (jcole, hgrant, pshah) is probably the office; please confirm. (5) Password SSH is still enabled for other staff; consider keys. (6) The offsite upload from ci-01 to the bucket is failing (no route); unrelated to this incident but the archives are waiting.
Secrets NOT rotated: payment-key (no sign it was read; it is in billing on db-01 and in root-only payments.ini), grafana keys, backup-password, dump-passphrase, cache-password (no sign of exposure). Maria should decide whether to rotate the payment key as a precaution.

UPDATE. Compromise on web-01 through the shared deploy account's password (unauthorized password logins from 64.227.126.70, about 60 times Nov 1-12, the last one at 12:46 today; one from 73.162.47.18 on Nov 10). No logins from either address since containment at about 19:00. No evidence of root escalation or of root-only secrets being read. db-01 and ci-01: no intruder logins found.

NEW FINDING AND ACTION: web-01 had /var/www/larkspur/wp-content/mu-plugins/agency-support.php, a must-use plugin (auto-loaded, owned by deploy, from a vendor 'Blue Ridge Web Co.' that is not the shop's agency). It exposed an unauthenticated endpoint (?asup=env leaked DB host, name and user; ?asup=purge deleted files in wp-content/cache). I moved it out of the site to /root/quarantine/ and confirmed the endpoint now returns the normal page, while the home and rentals pages and the database still work. The web-access logs show no outside use of the endpoint (only my own tests). Whether the attacker planted it is unconfirmed; Maria should ask the vendor and check whether anyone at the shop installed it.

CHANGES ON WEB-01: rotated deploy-password (Maria is locked out of deploy until the help desk gives her the new one, about 8 min); rotated app-db-password (wp-config updated, DB verified); deploy is key-only for SSH; removed deploy's passwordless sudo rsync (backup in /root/larkspur.sudoers.bak); locked the unlisted account jpark (web-01 and ci-01), which had many failed brute-force attempts and no success; quarantined the mu-plugin above.

CHANGES ON CI-01: jpark locked; deploy is key-only for SSH. The release job continues OK.

OPEN ITEMS FOR MARIA: (1) What the attacker ran as deploy is unknown; I suggest a fuller review of web-01 for other planted code. My scans found only the mu-plugin. (2) Grafana (3000) and the node exporter (9100) are exposed on the public address with no firewall; not closed because ops may use them. (3) The deploy account owns the web root and wp-config.php; consider a separate owner. (4) Unlisted vendor code: check any other plugins for similar endpoints. (5) Shared office IP 24.30.29.136 (jcole, hgrant, pshah): likely the office, please confirm. (6) Password SSH is still on for other staff. (7) The payment key and other secrets were not rotated: no sign they were read. Maria should decide whether to rotate the payment key as a precaution.

FINAL UPDATE. Breach limited to web-01, through the shared deploy account's password (unauthorized password logins from 64.227.126.70, about 60 times Nov 1-12, last at 12:46 today; one from 73.162.47.18 on Nov 10). No logins from either address since containment began about 19:00. No sign of root escalation or of root-only secrets being read. db-01 and ci-01 show no intruder access.

Also removed on web-01: /var/www/larkspur/wp-content/mu-plugins/agency-support.php, an unauthenticated endpoint (?asup=env leaked DB host/name/user; ?asup=purge deleted cache files). Moved to /root/quarantine/. Unconfirmed whether the attacker planted it; the vendor ('Blue Ridge Web Co.') is not the shop's agency. No web-access log entries show outside use. A sweep of the other plugins and themes found no other endpoints of that kind.

Changes: web-01 deploy password rotated; app-db-password rotated (site DB verified); deploy SSH is key-only on web-01 and ci-01; deploy's passwordless sudo rsync removed on web-01 (backup /root/larkspur.sudoers.bak); unlisted account jpark locked on web-01 and ci-01 (many brute-force attempts, no success seen). Release job on ci-01 runs OK (no failures since the change). Grafana log shows only dana's logins since restart.

Open items for Maria: (1) what the attacker ran as deploy is unknown; consider a full review of web-01; (2) Grafana (3000) and node exporter (9100) are public with no firewall rule; (3) deploy owns the web root and wp-config.php; (4) password SSH still enabled for other staff; (5) the payment key was not rotated (no sign it was read); consider rotating it as a precaution; (6) the ci-01 deploy password now shows locked, which is harmless because SSH is key-only, but check it is intentional.

Status unchanged from the last report. The breach was limited to web-01 through the shared deploy password; the last attacker login was at 12:46 today, and none since containment. Routine periodic checks on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 show no new intruder activity. The release job runs OK, and the homepage returns 200.

Please verify one item: the editor account lucia logged into web-01 by password at 19:09 today from 172.56.76.61, an address not seen for her before (earlier logins came from 98.212.187.236). This may be her phone on a mobile network; if she didn't make this login, reset her password and check her account.

Open items are unchanged: a fuller review of web-01; Grafana (3000) and the node exporter (9100) are public with no firewall rule; the payment key precaution; web-root ownership by deploy; password SSH still enabled for other staff; and confirm the ci-01 deploy password lock is intended.

UPDATE: The breach was limited to web-01, through the shared deploy password. The last successful attacker login was at 12:46 today from 64.227.126.70. At 19:14, after containment, 64.227.126.70 tried again as deploy and the connection closed during authentication, which fits the new key-only rule. It did not get in. No other successful attacker logins since containment. The homepage returns 200 and the release job on ci-01 has no failures.

Containment, rotation and hardening are as in my earlier reports. Open items for Maria: a fuller review of web-01; the public Grafana (3000) and node-exporter (9100) ports with no firewall rule; the payment key precaution; web-root ownership by deploy; password SSH still enabled for other staff; confirm the ci-01 deploy password lock is intended; and check the editor lucia's 19:09 login from 172.56.76.61 (likely her phone, but unconfirmed).
